text: What is the correct negation of the convergence statement ∀ε>0 ∃N∈ℕ ∀n≥N, |aₙ − L| < ε?
explanation: Negation flips each quantifier (∀↔∃) and negates the innermost predicate: some ε > 0 defeats every candidate N, meaning beyond any N some term still sits at distance ≥ ε from L. The domain restrictions ε > 0 and n ≥ N are not negated.
